normal_flow_topology_draft.summary: The topology represents a complex hospital discharge workflow. It includes routine discharge preparation, medication-related activities, home-care coordination, facility transfers, transport alternatives, discharge postponement, return to active treatment and discharge against medical advice.

nodes.name: Confirm preliminary clinical readiness
nodes.description: The responsible physician performs an initial assessment and determines whether the patient may enter the discharge preparation process.

nodes.name: Determine discharge disposition
nodes.description: The clinical team determines whether the planned discharge can continue, whether the patient must return to active treatment, or whether the patient intends to leave against medical advice.

nodes.name: Assess discharge complexity
nodes.description: The team identifies the clinical documentation, medication and continuity-of-care workstreams required for the discharge.

nodes.name: Prepare routine clinical documentation
nodes.description: The clinical team prepares the standard discharge letter, follow-up instructions, clinical reports and required certificates.

nodes.name: Perform medication reconciliation
nodes.description: Current medicines are compared with the intended post-discharge therapy to identify additions, discontinuations, substitutions and potential interactions.

nodes.name: Assess social and continuity-of-care needs
nodes.description: The team evaluates whether the patient can return home, requires organized home support, needs placement in another facility or currently has no safe discharge destination.

nodes.name: Finalize internal medication plan
nodes.description: The physician and hospital pharmacist finalize the post-discharge medication plan using resources available within the hospital.

nodes.name: Obtain external medication authorization
nodes.description: The team requests authorization or availability confirmation for medicines that require external approval, special dispensing or territorial pharmacy coordination.

nodes.name: Complete core discharge documentation
nodes.description: The standard clinical documents are reviewed for completeness and prepared for inclusion in the final discharge package.

nodes.name: Finalize medication plan
nodes.description: The final medication list, prescriptions, dispensing instructions and patient-facing medication information are completed.

nodes.name: Coordinate home support
nodes.description: Home nursing, caregiver availability, equipment delivery and community follow-up services are coordinated for a patient returning home.

nodes.name: Secure rehabilitation or long-term care placement
nodes.description: The team identifies a receiving facility, sends the clinical request and waits for an available bed and formal acceptance.

nodes.name: Identify unsafe discharge destination
nodes.description: The assessment concludes that neither home discharge nor immediate facility transfer is currently safe or operationally possible.

nodes.name: Assemble clinical discharge package
nodes.description: Clinical documentation and the finalized medication plan are combined into the complete clinical discharge package.

nodes.name: Confirm home-care readiness
nodes.description: The responsible team confirms that the home environment, caregiver support, equipment and community services are ready.

nodes.name: Confirm receiving-facility readiness
nodes.description: The receiving facility confirms acceptance, bed availability, admission timing and any transfer-specific requirements.

nodes.name: Initiate safeguarding and bed-management escalation
nodes.description: The case is escalated to social services, safeguarding personnel and bed management because a safe discharge destination is unavailable.

nodes.name: Confirm home discharge readiness
nodes.description: The clinical discharge package and the required home-care arrangements are considered ready for final departure planning.

nodes.name: Confirm facility transfer readiness
nodes.description: The clinical discharge package and receiving-facility acceptance are considered sufficient to organize the inter-facility transfer.

nodes.name: Prepare independent departure
nodes.description: The patient is considered capable of leaving independently without organized transportation.

nodes.name: Coordinate family or caregiver pickup
nodes.description: The patient departure time is coordinated with a family member or caregiver who will accompany the patient home.

nodes.name: Arrange medical transport
nodes.description: A medical transport provider is booked because the patient requires supervised or assisted transportation.

nodes.name: Prepare inter-facility handoff
nodes.description: The hospital prepares the patient, documentation, medication and operational information required for transfer to another facility.

nodes.name: Verify standard departure
nodes.description: Staff verify patient identity, documentation delivery, prescriptions, instructions and the presence of the expected accompanying person when applicable.

nodes.name: Complete medical transport handoff
nodes.description: The patient is handed over to the transport crew together with the necessary clinical information, equipment and transport instructions.

nodes.name: Transmit transfer dossier
nodes.description: The complete transfer dossier is transmitted to the receiving facility through the agreed digital, paper or mixed communication channel.

nodes.name: Close administrative hospitalization episode
nodes.description: The hospital records the departure or transfer, updates bed availability and closes the administrative hospitalization episode.

nodes.name: Complete transport documentation
nodes.description: Transport-specific documentation and departure timestamps are recorded after the patient has been handed over to the medical transport crew.

nodes.name: Handle denied or unavailable medication authorization
nodes.description: The requested medicine cannot be authorized, supplied or made available within the timeframe required for discharge.

nodes.name: Return patient to active treatment
nodes.description: A new clinical issue, deterioration or unresolved diagnostic concern causes the patient to return to active inpatient treatment.

nodes.name: Place discharge on operational hold
nodes.description: The discharge process is formally paused while a safe destination, legal arrangement or appropriate support solution is sought.

nodes.name: Process discharge against medical advice
nodes.description: The patient decides to leave despite the clinical team's recommendation to remain in care, triggering a dedicated risk-documentation process.

nodes.name: Confirm receiving-facility acceptance
nodes.description: The receiving facility confirms receipt of the dossier and accepts operational responsibility for the arriving patient.

nodes.name: Complete planned discharge or transfer
nodes.description: The patient has left the hospital through the planned home-discharge or inter-facility transfer path, and the hospitalization episode is closed.

nodes.name: Postpone discharge pending medication access
nodes.description: The planned discharge is postponed because safe access to a required post-discharge medicine cannot be guaranteed.

nodes.name: Cancel current discharge attempt
nodes.description: The current discharge attempt is closed and the patient remains admitted under an active treatment plan.

nodes.name: Continue hospitalization pending safe destination
nodes.description: The patient remains hospitalized because no safe and operationally valid discharge destination is currently available.

nodes.name: Patient leaves against medical advice
nodes.description: The patient leaves after receiving risk information and after the hospital records the refusal of the recommended treatment or continued hospitalization.

clarification_questions.question: Are documentation, medication reconciliation and continuity-of-care assessment executed in parallel, or are they alternative paths selected according to discharge complexity?
clarification_questions.why_needed: Node mfp_003 has three outgoing connections, but the current topology does not distinguish parallel execution from mutually exclusive routing.

clarification_questions.question: Is external medication authorization required only for selected patients, and what condition determines whether the workflow follows mfp_007, mfp_008 or both?
clarification_questions.why_needed: The medication branch may represent optional work, alternative work or parallel work, and the current graph does not encode that distinction.

clarification_questions.question: Can the clinical discharge package be considered complete before home-care or receiving-facility readiness is confirmed?
clarification_questions.why_needed: The graph converges clinical preparation with destination-specific readiness at two different points, but the precise synchronization rule is unclear.

clarification_questions.question: Does a denied external medication authorization always postpone discharge, or can the clinical team substitute the medicine and return to the main medication path?
clarification_questions.why_needed: The current branch terminates at postponed discharge, but a substitution or escalation loop may exist in the real workflow.

clarification_questions.question: At what exact moment does responsibility transfer to the receiving facility: dossier receipt, explicit acceptance or physical patient arrival?
clarification_questions.why_needed: The transfer branch contains several possible handoff points that may belong to different operational or legal boundaries.

clarification_questions.question: Should discharge against medical advice reuse any standard documentation or administrative closure activities from the planned discharge path?
clarification_questions.why_needed: The current topology models the against-medical-advice path as an independent terminal branch, but some documentation and closure steps may be shared.
